meta.description: Teach your child to tell real expertise from authority manipulation. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: "I'm older, so I'm right!" — and your child agrees without understanding why?
hero.subheadline: Instead of arguments — status. "I'm older" is not a reason. It's authority manipulation.

media.alt: A child under authority pressure, being told what to do without explanation

pain.title: Age and role are not proof of being right
pain.body:
"I'm older — I know better", "listen to the adults", "you're too young to decide that". At school, at home, among older children. The child might have doubts — but agrees, because authority carries its own weight. Not through arguments, but through status.

This isn't real expertise — it's authority manipulation: instead of evidence, a role is used — "I'm older, so I'm right". But age or position don't guarantee correctness. Without the skill to recognise this, the child stops checking and simply agrees.

The result — decisions are made not because they understood, but because "that's what they were told". Gradually they get used to not asking questions where it's "expected" to just trust.

solution.body: 40 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to protect themselves.
bullets: 🔍 Tells real expertise apart from empty "I know better"

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.
